weak.claim: Measured AC efficiency is modest. The Solar Lab got 27 min at a 1,779 W load, which it rates as 79% efficiency. Arithmetic: 1,779 W x 0.45 h = about 800 Wh delivered from 1,024 Wh.
The surge rating overstates what it actually delivers. The Solar Lab saw voltage drop during surges, 'reducing power delivery instead of momentarily exceeding its 2,000W rating'.
The fan is loud. Mark Wolfe (Bob Vila) found the wall-charging fan noticeably louder than on other stations he has tested. The Solar Lab calls it 'very, very loud'. Neither gave a dB figure.
Measured wall charging was slower than the advertised 36 min. Bob Vila measured 'less than 1.5 hours' on AC. The 36-min claim uses 2,200 W combined AC and solar input; AC alone is 1,400 W max.
Heavier than its lighter rivals: 27.8 lb, against 25 lb for the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and 23.8 lb for the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2.
Slower UPS switchover than its rivals: under 20 ms, against 10 ms or less on BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic.
Lower solar input than the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: 800 W max (12-78 V, 14 A) against 1,000 W.
Expansion ceiling is lower than Jackery's. The Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 scales to 11 kWh; the Mega 1 tops out at 5.12 kWh.
The OUPES store charges $210 more than Amazon for the same unit ($699 vs $489), so the maker store is the worse place to buy.

wins_for: Home-outage buyers who want 2,000 W at about $500 and may grow to 3-5 kWh later
Shoppers who need to run one 1,800-2,000 W appliance, such as a microwave, kettle or space heater
Buyers pricing about 3 kWh of backup: the OUPES 3,072 Wh kit on Amazon works out to $0.42/Wh (arithmetic)
not_for: Carrying it to camp: the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (25 lb) or Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (23.8 lb) is lighter
Quiet bedrooms or overnight CPAP use: reviewers call the fan loud. BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 claims 30 dB and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic claims 30 dB or less at 600 W (maker claims)
PCs, NAS boxes and other UPS-sensitive gear: switchover is under 20 ms, against 10 ms or less on BLUETTI, Jackery and EcoFlow
Solar-first charging: the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 takes 1,000 W of solar
Growing past 5 kWh or running a whole house: the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 scales to 11 kWh, and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Plus has a 3,600 W inverter
Lowest price for 1 kWh: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic is $459 and the PECRON E1000LFP is $399 on Amazon, both 1,800 W

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Lighter (25 lb), 1,000 W solar input, UPS switchover of 10 ms or less, 4,000+ cycles, 30 dB claim
23.8 lb; expands to 11 kWh; UPS under 10 ms; under 30 dB in Silent Mode (maker claim)
$30 cheaper than the Mega 1 on Amazon; 10 ms auto-switch; 30 dB or less at 600 W (maker claim)
240 Wh more base capacity, also expands to 5 kWh, 4,000 cycles

Same Amazon price with more ratings (1,403 vs 370), but its store listing names 9 ports and no expansion, against 13 outputs and expansion to 5.12 kWh on the Mega 1. Easy to confuse with the Mega 1, so link the exact ASIN.
